issues.failure_explanation: Every map f and every subspace V admit the decomposition f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}, so as stated the proposition covers all manifolds. But sec:lem_enc shows the linear encoder is injective on M only when f_V is invertible (equivalently J_{\Psi'} is injective on M); without that hypothesis points of M are identified and ε₁ ≠ 0. The paper's own perturbed-coil example is a manifold of exactly the stated form f = f_V + f_{V^\perp} for which the source states a non-linear encoder is necessary, contradicting the proposition as written.

failure_location.quote: (A linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ manifolds described by $f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}$)\textbf{.}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis that f_V is invertible (J_{\Psi'} injective on M), as required by sec:lem_enc; the reconstruction conclusion then follows from the given argument.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition, and the summary claim that it 'justifies the use of a linear encoder', cover a strictly larger class of manifolds than is information-preserving; only manifolds on which the projection to V is injective are supported.
issues.title: Linear–non-linear autoencoder claim omits injectivity of f_V
issues.why_classification: A one-clause hypothesis addition restores the statement for exactly the class already treated in sec:lem_enc and in the examples, with no change to method, conclusion or scope beyond the added condition.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We call $n$ the latent size, $\Psi':\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^n$, $m\leq n<N$, the encoder, and $\Psi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^N$ the decoder.
there is a ReLU neural network $N_f$ with input dimension $n_{\text{in}}$, hidden layer widths at most $w$, and output dimension $n_{\text{out}}$ that $\varepsilon$-approximates $f$:
This theorem leads to the following proposition about fully non-linear autoencoders.

issues.failure_explanation: The only support offered is the universal approximation theorem, which gives ε-approximation of continuous maps, not an injective encoder together with a decoder satisfying Ψ∘Ψ' = id_M. In the standing range m ≤ n < N the statement is also false: an m-manifold such as the real projective plane does not embed in R^n for n = m or n < 4, so no injective Ψ' into such a latent space exists. No embedding existence argument and no extension of the inverse to a continuous decoder is supplied.

failure_location.quote: A non-linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ generic manifolds\textbf{.}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to manifolds admitting a topological embedding in R^n (e.g. n ≥ 2a+1-style bound from th:latent_dim) and add the missing argument that the inverse of the embedding extends to a continuous decoder (Tietze), leaving th:uap to supply only ε₂ → 0.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised capability of fully non-linear autoencoders to give null representation error on 'generic manifolds' is unproved and, at the latent sizes the section allows, false; only manifolds embedding in R^n are covered.
issues.title: Exact reproduction of generic manifolds is asserted without argument and false at the stated latent sizes
issues.why_classification: The statement must be requantified and a nontrivial existence construction (embedding plus continuous decoder) supplied; the qualitative conclusion for embeddable manifolds survives, so no global loss occurs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To ensure the injectivity of the encoder approximated by a neural network, each layer must be injective, condition which is satisfied when $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers, so $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$ for $\ell = 1,\ldots,L-1$.
By \Cref{th:uap}, we have that $n_\ell = n_\text{in}+n_\text{out}$ is sufficient to satisfy $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ and $\lim_{|\myw|\to\infty}\Varepsilon_2 = 0$.
Note that this study is independent of the specific activation function used.

issues.failure_explanation: n_ℓ ≥ n_{ℓ-1} is at best a necessary dimensional condition: a layer σ(W·+b) with n_ℓ ≥ n_{ℓ-1} need not be injective (rank-deficient W has a kernel; ReLU identifies vectors agreeing in their positive parts), so the key inference is false and the claim of activation-independence is false as well. The appeal to th:uap is invalid twice over: it bounds the minimal width of arbitrarily deep networks that ε-approximate continuous functions, not the injectivity of a single layer, and uniform approximation does not preserve injectivity, so it cannot deliver ε₁ = 0. Even with injective hidden layers, injectivity of the final reduction R^{n_{L-1}} → R^n on the reshaped manifold requires an embedding/realizability argument that is absent.

failure_location.quote: A sufficient condition for the width to ensure injectivity of the encoder is $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$, for $\ell = 1,\ldots, L-1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the condition with the missing hypotheses (componentwise injective activations and full-column-rank weights, so each hidden layer is injective) and replace the proof by an argument that at latent size n at least the embedding dimension of M some network parameters make the whole encoder injective on M (embedding plus an injectivity-preserving realization), treating ε₂ → 0 separately with th:uap.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised architectural guarantee (reduce only at the last layer with hidden widths ≥ n_in to obtain null representation error), the remark warning against progressive narrowing, and the width choices used to design the networks in the numerical tests are unsupported.
issues.title: Layer width does not ensure injectivity of the encoder
issues.why_classification: The statement and its central proof step are false, but a corrected version with standard extra hypotheses and one contained embedding/realizability argument keeps the last-layer reduction rule, the width guidance and ε₁ = 0; no new global architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This property can be achieved, for example, constructing the decoder as $J_\Psi = (J_{\Psi'}^\top J_{\Psi'})^{-1}J_{\Psi'}^\top$, which can be enforced in the optimization process (see \Cref{sec:train}) by adding the following loss contribution: $\mathcal{N}_{ij} = \| (J_{\Psi'}^\top J_{\Psi'})J_{\Psi} - J_{\Psi'}^\top\|^2$.
Therefore, the eigenvalues $\neq 0$ are those of $\Lambda$, so the bound on the timestep of the \node\ is, in the worst scenario, the same as that of the \Node.

issues.failure_explanation: For an idempotent P = J_ΨJ_{Ψ'} the nonzero eigenvalues of PΛ are those of the compression of Λ to range(P), which are eigenvalues of Λ only if range(J_Ψ) is Λ-invariant; invariance is neither assumed nor proved. Counterexample inside the model problem and the exact linear-reduction setting: Λ = [[-1,100,0],[0,-1,0],[0,100,-2]] is Hurwitz (eigenvalues -1,-1,-2) and trajectories from u_0 = (μ,0,0) form the linear manifold on the x-axis, reproduced exactly by J_Ψ = [e_1 | (0,1,1)^T], J_{Ψ'} = [[1,0,0],[0,1/2,1/2]], for which J_ΨJ_{Ψ'} is exactly the orthogonal projector required in the paragraph; yet A = J_{Ψ'}ΛJ_Ψ = [[-1,100],[0,48.5]] has the positive eigenvalue 48.5, so the reduced Forward Euler scheme is unstable for every Δ t while the N-ODE decays. Independently, the proposed construction is ill-typed: (J_{Ψ'}^T J_{Ψ'})^{-1}J_{Ψ'}^T is n×N while J_Ψ must be N×n, and the penalty ‖(J_{Ψ'}^T J_{Ψ'})J_Ψ - J_{Ψ'}^T‖² multiplies an n×n by an N×n matrix, which is undefined.

failure_location.quote: Due to the specific assumptions made in the construction of the decoder, the projection sets some eigenvalues to zero while leaving the others unchanged.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to autoencoders whose latent subspace is invariant under Λ (true when the exact linear reduction is minimal, span(M) = col(J_Ψ), since then Λu is tangent to M on M) and prove that invariance, and replace the pseudoinverse formula and penalty by the correctly typed J_Ψ = J_{Ψ'}^T(J_{Ψ'}J_{Ψ'}^T)^{-1} with matching loss.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that for orthogonal-projection autoencoders the FE stability bound of the n-ODE is no worse than that of the N-ODE is false as quantified and its derivation is invalid; the proposed decoder construction/penalty is not a well-defined map or loss, and the analogous conclusion for linear encoders with non-linear decoders (linearisation about u_n = 0) inherits the defect.
issues.title: Projection does not preserve the eigenvalues of Λ, so the timestep-bound claim fails
issues.why_classification: Recovering the conclusion needs a new hypothesis with a short new invariance argument and a corrected construction; the general claim for arbitrary orthogonal-projection autoencoders must be dropped, but the minimal exact-reduction case remains, so the loss is limited.

\mathscr{N}_{ij}^3 = &\Bigg\| \sum_{p=0}^P \alpha_p\left( \Psi'(u_{N}(t_{j+1-p})+\zeta_{j+1-p}) + \kappa(u_{N}(t_{j+1-p})+\zeta_{j+1-p})\right) + \

It follows that a necessary condition for $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\|J_{N_{\Psi'}}(t_k)-J_{\Psi'}(t_k)\|_\infty \to 0$, therefore, an accurate representation of the encoder and its Jacobian is necessary.

issues.failure_explanation: Equating the loss to zero and 'comparing' with eq:diff_op_tau cannot give pointwise agreement of N_{F_n} and F_n: the two relations involve the encoder and the data at P+1 different time levels, and consistency (Σ_p α_p = 0) makes κ and ζ enter only through their one-step increments. For FE the relation forced by the two equations is N_{F_n} - F_n = τ_n + (∇κ)F_N + O(increment of ζ per step), i.e. the error is governed by the derivative of the encoder error amplified by 1/Δ t, not by ‖κ‖. Hence κ → 0 is not sufficient (κ_δ with ‖κ_δ‖ = δ → 0 but ‖∇κ_δ‖ → ∞ makes the learned right-hand side error unbounded) and not necessary (for constant F_n the trained network equals F_n exactly whatever a non-vanishing constant κ, which cancels from the residual because Σ_p α_p = 0). The correct control (C¹/one-step increment bounds on κ and ζ) is exactly what the source itself demands only for the semi data-driven case.

failure_location.quote: A necessary condition to meet the requirement $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots} \|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\tau_n^k, \zeta_k \to 0$ and $\kappa \to 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the comparison by a valid one-step error identity (N_{F_n} - F_n = τ_n + (∇κ)F_N + O(ζ-increments)) and state sufficient conditions controlling the one-step increments of κ and ζ (e.g. C¹ bounds vanishing as |w| → ∞, Δ t_train → 0); withdraw or correct the 'necessary condition' statement. With these conditions the convergence claim and its use in th:global_convergence go through.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee that the fully data-driven loss drives N_{F_n} → F_n is unestablished, and with it the step of th:global_convergence that concludes ε_{F_n}(Δ t_train, w) → 0 for this training strategy; the convergence claim of the main theorem holds only under stronger, unstated conditions on the encoder error.
issues.title: Convergence of the fully data-driven training rests on an invalid comparison
issues.why_classification: The advertised conclusion (convergence of the fully data-driven training) is recoverable with a corrected contained argument and stronger but comparable conditions; only the necessity claim must be weakened, so no new global proof architecture or major loss is forced.

issues.failure_explanation: The losses are means of squared, unnormalised 2-norms, so a loss of 10^{-3} corresponds to a root-mean-square error of about 3·10^{-2} in absolute terms, not to a relative error of 10^{-3}. The inference drops the square root and reports an absolute error as relative (and the combined loss additionally mixes the errors in u_N and in F_n with user-chosen weights), overstating the attained accuracy by more than an order of magnitude.
